paths.description: Homepage: primary news discovery surface and shared global navigation/chrome.
Business news listing: representative section/index template.
Lead subscriber article: representative article/detail and paywall template.
Search for AI: representative query and results journey.
Login redirect to NIKKEI ID: representative authentication form and passkey/autocomplete inspection.
Unknown route: representative HTTP/navigation failure recovery state.

findings.summary: A consent prompt obscures primary news content on initial load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a large consent panel over the lead story; on mobile it covers roughly the lower third of the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface where lawful, preserve equal Reject/Agree actions, and keep content readable.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size, and the interaction probe found numerous visible links only 13–23px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24×24 CSS px targets with adequate spacing, preferably 44px for primary mobile controls.

findings.summary: Lab LCP misses the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.0s and Speed Index 6.9s; the independent trace measured LCP 2.15s, showing variable but material load risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the lead image/content, reduce third-party competition, and validate LCP under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Some links lack discernible accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and the DOM probe found multiple visible image-only article links without direct text/ARIA naming; the images audit reported 31 missing alt values, including decorative and potentially meaningful images.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive link a computed accessible name and provide meaningful alt text while using empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Some text does not meet minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens until text and essential UI meet WCAG contrast thresholds.

findings.summary: The homepage has a large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 12 third-party origins including Facebook and Google Tag Manager; HAR attributes 59 requests and 1.34MB to non-main origins before consent interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential trackers on consent, remove low-value vendors, minimize events, and batch analytics.

findings.summary: Article identity and much rendered content are missing from the raw no-JavaScript representation.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 32% overlap for the representative article; its rendered title and h1 were absent from raw HTML. Homepage overlap was 43%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render article title, heading and core text; hydrate enhancement behavior without replacing crawlable content.

findings.summary: Third-party transfer is disproportionate for a text-first news homepage.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins account for 1.34MB of 1.65MB total transferred; the CMP alone transferred about 500KB across its origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party byte/request budget, slim the CMP, and defer analytics/ad code.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is visually identical to the light page; the probe reports colorScheme "normal", body text rgb(51,51,51), and no color-scheme media rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide dark surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not explicitly supported and ordinary contrast defects remain.
findings.evidence: The preference CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, and Lighthouse failed its color-contrast audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations and correct failing text/background color pairs.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is not exposed as a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no dialog, role=dialog, or popover while the screenshot shows modal-like overlay content delivered through a third-party iframe.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose modal semantics, focus management, accessible naming, Escape handling, and platform dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is request-heavy and includes weak cache hygiene.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 113 requests and 1.65MB transferred; it identified an uncached 66.9KB campaign image and multiple high-priority tracking scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Cache immutable assets, defer non-critical tracking/consent dependencies, and keep the critical request chain focused on lead content.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the transferred payload.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 59 requests and 1.34MB, about 81% of transfer, to non-main origins; Lighthouse also reports missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit and conditionally load analytics/CMP integrations; remove duplicate or low-value tags and ship source maps privately or publicly as policy allows.

findings.summary: Reflow succeeds, but target sizing remains inadequate.
findings.evidence: The 360px layout has no horizontal overflow, but Lighthouse failed target-size and the probe recorded many controls below 24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the fluid reflow and enlarge/space interactive hit areas without disabling user scaling.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console; HAR also recorded failed Facebook, ad, tag-manager and ORB-blocked tracking requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or guard failed integrations and keep expected third-party failures from surfacing as page errors.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery have widespread sizing/efficiency defects.
findings.evidence: The image probe reports 95 of 100 images without width/height attributes, 35 oversized images, 82 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 43 legacy-format assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and prefer AVIF/WebP where appropriate.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors even though the viewport meta and most sampled navigation links use real href values.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace JavaScript-only or malformed navigation targets with real href URLs and keep descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP posture has avoidable weaknesses.
findings.evidence: The cookie probe found lux_uid without Secure and a 400-day analytics cookie; the response CSP only sets frame-ancestors while a meta CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval across a very broad origin list.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, shorten nonessential retention, and deploy an enforceable nonce/hash-based response CSP.

findings.summary: Image assets are frequently oversized or delivered in legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 35 oversized images, 43 legacy-format images and 6 without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes and optimize decorative campaign assets.

findings.summary: Non-content background integrations perform substantial work on initial load.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 59 third-party requests while Lighthouse reported forced reflow and the page loaded multiple analytics/tracking integrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer background analytics until idle/consent, batch events, and remove integrations without measurable reader value.

findings.summary: Repeated menu interaction correlates with retained heap growth and needs leak investigation.
findings.evidence: After 10 open/close cycles, the heap summary rose from 22.64MB/310,078 nodes to 24.30MB/330,095 nodes (about 7% bytes and 6.5% nodes). Separate browser sessions lower confidence, but constructor counts also rose.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the menu/CMP lifecycle in one session with baseline-target-final snapshots; remove retained listeners, timers, nodes or caches.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps are abrupt.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no authored view-transition rules while the representative navigation is an MPA with page-to-page route changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use @view-transition { navigation: auto } with reduced-motion-safe shared-element treatment for stable global chrome.

findings.summary: Reusable components rely on viewport styling rather than container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The CSS capability probe found no authored @container rules despite cards and navigation components appearing in multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reused card/list modules where their layout depends on available component width.

findings.summary: DevTools reports browser-platform hygiene issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed inspector-issues and valid-source-maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools Issues findings and publish usable source maps according to the site’s debugging/security policy.

findings.summary: The homepage has a relatively large live heap/DOM footprint for its initial state.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contains 310,078 nodes and 22.64MB self size before deliberate interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial DOM/card population, virtualize or defer below-fold modules, and trim third-party object graphs.
